column1: # go-to-rust-crates.tsv — declarative Go-package -> Rust-crate map for the
# When a converted Sky project carries a `["go.dependencies"]` section, the
# looks up each Go import path here and, for a real crates.io crate, emits it
# under `[rust.dependencies]` in the generated ipe.toml — the section the Ipê FFI
#   2  rust-crate         crates.io crate name + version spec, OR one of the
#                         sentinels below. A `{...}` value carries cargo features
#                         and is emitted verbatim as an inline table.
#   3  confidence         `mapped`   — a reviewed, honest crates.io equivalent
#                         `stdlib`   — covered by Ipê's own stdlib / Rust std;
#                                      NO crate dependency is emitted (the Ipê
#                                      marker so a human confirms it, never a
#   4  note               short human rationale (why this crate / why stdlib)
# HONESTY RULE (PRINCIPLES.md §Security, §0): a mapping we are not sure of is
# marked `unsure`, never asserted as `mapped`. A Go crate with a stronger safety
# or capability guarantee than its nearest Rust crate is flagged in the note, not
# silently downgraded. Adding a row is the whole registration — the converter
# reads this file, nothing is hard-coded.
# The seed rows come from 13-skyshop, whose committed override
# `[rust.dependencies]` block is the source of the skyshop mappings below.
# ── Go standard library — covered by Ipê stdlib / Rust std, no crate needed ──
